n: *Translator's note:* *Heb* “and they lifted up their voice[s] and wept with great weeping.” Both the cognate accusative בְּכִי (bekhi, “weeping”) and the attributive adjective גָדוֹל (gadol, “great”) emphasize their degree of sorrow.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “A great oath there was concerning the one who did not go up before the Lord at Mizpah, saying, ‘He must surely be put to death.’”

*Translator's note:* Or “felt sorry for.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “cut off one.”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “What should we do for them, for the remaining ones, concerning wives?”
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Look, no one had come to the camp from Jabesh Gilead to the assembly.”

*Translator's note:* Or “when the people were mustered.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and look.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “men, sons of strength.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “there.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “the edge of the sword.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “And this is the thing that you will do.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “a knower of the bed of a male.” The verb יָדָע (yadaʿ) “to know,” “be intimate with,” is used as a euphemism for sexual relations.

*Text-critical note:* Some Greek witnesses (notably Codex Vaticanus [B]) add the words, “‘But the virgins you should keep alive.’ And they did so.” These additional words, which probably represent the original Hebrew text, can be retroverted: וְאֶת־הַבְּתוּלוֹת תְּחַיּוּ וַיַּעֲשׂוּ כֵן (veʾet habbetulot tekhayyu vayyaʿasu khen). It is likely that a scribe’s eye jumped from the ו (vav) on וְאֶת (veʾet) to the initial vav of v. {{Judges 21:11|11}}, accidentally leaving out the intervening letters. The present translation is based on this reconstruction.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “who were not knowers of a man by the bed of a male.” The verb יָדַע (yadaʿ) “to know,” or “to be intimate with,” acts as a euphemism for sexual relations, which is further clarified by reference to a man’s bed.
*Translator's note:* *Heb* “And all the assembly sent and spoke to the sons of Benjamin who were at the cliff of Rimmon and they proclaimed to them peace.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “they”; the referent (the Israelites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “but they did not find for them enough.”

*Translator's note:* Or “felt sorry for.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “had made a gaping hole in.” The narrator uses imagery that compares Israel to a wall that has been breached.

*Translator's note:* Or “elders.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “What should we do for the remaining ones concerning wives?”

*Translator's note:* The Hebrew text has “and they said” at the beginning of the verse. For stylistic reasons the translation treats v. {{Judges 21:17|17}} as a continuation of the remarks of the leaders in v. {{Judges 21:16|16}}.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “An inheritance for the remnant belonging to Benjamin, and a tribe from Israel will not be wiped away.” The first statement lacks a verb. Some prefer to emend the text to read, “How can an inheritance remain for the remnant of Benjamin?”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “But we are not able to give to them wives from our daughters.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “is cursed.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and look.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and look, when.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “in the dances.”

*Text-critical note:* The (original) LXX and Vulgate read “to you.”

*Translator's note:* The words “and let them be” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “for we did not take each his wife in battle.”

*Study note:* *Through battle*. This probably refers to the battle against Jabesh Gilead, which only produced 400 of the 600 wives needed.

*Translator's note:* This sentence is not in the Hebrew text. It is supplied in the translation to clarify the logic of the statement.

*Text-critical note:* *Heb* “You did not give to them, now you are guilty.” The MT as it stands makes little sense. It is preferable to emend לֹא (loʾ, “not”) to לוּא (luʾ, “if”). This particle introduces a purely hypothetical condition, “If you had given to them [but you didn’t].” See G. F. Moore, *Judges* (ICC), 453-54.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “did so.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “And they took wives according to their number from the dancing girls whom they abducted.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “went and returned.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “inheritance.”

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “and lived in them.”

*Study note:* *Each man did what he considered to be right*. The Book of Judges closes with this note, which summarizes the situation of the Israelite tribes during this period.

*Translator's note:* *Heb* “Each was doing what was right in his [own] eyes.”
